newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb judge refuses to open next hearing.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb judge refuses to open next hearing.

text.p: The judge in the Oklahoma City bombing case on Friday refused a news media request to conduct discussions of jury selection and other pre-trial issues in public next week.
U.S. District Judge Richard Matsch did, however, order some previously sealed court documents to be unsealed.

As far as next week's closed court conference, Matsch said the issues to be discussed between him, prosecutors and attorneys for defendant Timothy McVeigh were trial-planning matters typically done behind closed doors.
McVeigh and former Army buddy Terry Nichols are awaiting trial for the April 19, 1995, bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people.

A coalition of print and broadcast news media had objected to the meeting, arguing that the judge was wrong in conducting closed court proceedings and allowing numerous documents in the case to be sealed.

But the judge on Friday ordered some previously sealed material to be unsealed. One document showed that McVeigh's lawyers accused the federal government of trying to "conceal and destroy" evidence that would help McVeigh.

A spokeswoman for prosecutors said that claim "has been repeatedly rejected" by the trial judge. The allegation was made as part of a defence request to suppress the testimoney of what they called "a key government witness" against McVeigh.
The witness, a manager of an auto repair store in Junction City, Kansas, said he sold McVeigh the car he was driving when he was arrested soon after the bombing.
McVeigh's attorneys want the manager's incriminating comments suppressed. They claim an earlier statement he made to authorities indicated someone other than McVeigh committed the bombing.
McVeigh's defence team alleges prosecutors failed to disclose that the witness until recently left out details of McVeigh's movements in the shop when he bought the vehicle.
The McVeigh team has asserted that authorities have the wrong man in custody.
McVeigh's trial was to begin on March 31. Nichols will be tried separately at an undetermined later date.
